item.title: Version 1.2.0
item.description:
• Say a thought without typing it. Hold Shift with the talk key and Slate keeps the words instead of putting them in the app you are in. A separate key opens a short list of your newest notes and your last few dictations, and the one you pick is typed at your cursor. Notes stay on this Mac until you delete them, and Settings has the full list.
  • Dictate a numbered list and get one. Say "one, milk, two, eggs, three, bread" and it comes out as a list. If the pauses are not landing where you want them, say the word "comma" between the parts instead and it works every time.
  • A list only happens when you meant one. Counting, quantities, prices, clock times, decimals and version numbers all stay as ordinary sentences.

item.title: Version 1.1.7
item.description:
• Setup is five short steps, and it waits for the microphone and Accessibility instead of letting you past them. Skipping those was how Slate ended up installed and silent, with the talk key doing nothing and no explanation on screen.
  • Setup also shows you the dictionary and the history, which people were only finding by accident.
  • Spoken single quotes. Say “apostrophe” and “close apostrophe” around something and you get the marks, and “quote … unquote” works too.
  • A new setting keeps the last dictation on the clipboard, so you can paste it again yourself. It is off unless you turn it on.
  • The speech model downloads in the background while you set Slate up, rather than making you wait on a screen of its own.

item.title: Version 1.1.6
item.description:
• Saying “new paragraph” or “new line” works again after an ordinary phrase. In 1.1.5 a sentence like “Thanks for the update new paragraph…” typed the words out instead of making the break.
  • Saying “scratch that” in the middle of a sentence works again, and spoken email addresses join again.
  • A hands-free session ends on silence again instead of staying open.
  • If the speech model fails to load, pressing the talk key now retries properly instead of showing the same message every time.
  • Dictating twice in a row no longer repeats the last few words of the first take.

item.title: Version 1.1.5
item.description:
• Typing a character that needs the Right Option key, like the @ sign on a Spanish or German keyboard, no longer starts a recording. It also no longer throws away the sentence you had just finished.
  • Clipboard history apps like Maccy, Paste, and Alfred no longer keep a copy of everything you dictate. Slate now marks the text so those apps skip it.
  • Several cleanup rules were taking out words they should have left alone. "A brand new line of products" and "the very next line" stay as words. "Bora Bora" and "Duran Duran" keep both halves. Saying "scratch that" after a spoken paragraph break no longer reaches back too far.
  • Quiet speech is no longer cut off part way through a long sentence.
  • Cleanup runs faster, so your words land sooner after you let go of the key.

item.title: Version 1.1.4
item.description:
• The talk key starts at once. Slate keeps the microphone ready for a minute after you speak, so talking again does not wait for it to warm up. There is a switch for this in Settings under Speed.
  • The green marks in the live text now only appear on a word Slate went back and changed its mind about. They used to appear on words that had simply moved along the line.
  • Time saved counts the time you actually spent speaking, measured, instead of assuming everyone speaks at the same pace.

item.title: Version 1.1.3
item.description:
• When the talk key stops working, Slate now says so. The menu bar icon changes, and the menu tells you how to put it back.
  • Putting it back has a step that is easy to miss, so Slate spells it out: if Slate is already in the Accessibility list, take it out and add it again.
  • The welcome card no longer sits against the camera notch.

item.title: Version 1.1.2
item.description:
• Changing headphones mid sentence no longer cuts your words short. Slate waits for the new microphone and keeps going.
  • If the microphone does go away for good, Slate types what it heard instead of leaving the pill on screen.
  • Quitting Slate while your music is paused now starts the music again.

item.title: Version 1.1.1
item.description:
• New spoken commands: full stop, semicolon, next paragraph, closed brackets, and curly braces.
  • Adding words to the dictionary is simpler: say it on the left, get it on the right, press Return.
  • The setup card stays clear of the camera cutout, can be closed, and opens System Settings only once.
  • Anything dictated into a password field stays out of history.
  • Steadier long dictations, quicker auto-stop, and dozens of small fixes.

item.title: Version 1.1.0
item.description: • Slate can now update itself. The switch is in Settings › About, and it stays off until you turn it on.
